subject: Urgent: BrightCommerce streaming responses slowed — commitments & next steps
messages:
From: Emily Torres <emily.torres@brightcommerce.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Streaming responses slowed this morning

Jordan —

We saw a noticeable slowdown on our live chat widget starting around 08:45 PST. Responses from the model are taking 3–6 seconds between token chunks, and some requests are timing out. This is affecting checkout flows for about 15% of sessions (we've started failing over to cached responses but it's impacting conversion).

Two quick asks: can you confirm if this is on Redwood's side, and if you can provide a mitigation we can flip on from our end? I can share request IDs and a short capture if that helps.

Thanks,
Emily Torres
Director, Platform Ops — BrightCommerce

[attachment: client_capture_20271205.json (application/json) - 48KB]
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Emily Torres <emily.torres@brightcommerce.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-05T09:35:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Streaming responses slowed this morning

Emily — thanks for the quick heads-up and for the capture. We're seeing elevated token emission times across a small set of edge shards in us-west-2 that correspond to your sessions.

Immediate mitigation (already applied):
- Re-routed BrightCommerce traffic to a warm shard pool with lower load (reduces per-token latency variance).
- Enabled a short-lived token batching relax (reduces inter-token delay at the cost of tiny throughput impact).
- Deployed a hotfix that forces a lightweight KV cache check to avoid repeated cold cache hits for repeated prefixes.

From our telemetry: the service entered a pacing regime where some GRPC backpressure caused token spacing to widen. We're collecting detailed diagnostics and I'll attach the Redwood trace bundle shortly.

Two action items for your side (fast toggles):
1) If you can enable the client-side "graceful-dechunking" flag in the next 10–15 minutes we can reduce the visible jitter (we can provide a one-line config).
2) As a fallback, switch to model-redwood-medium for the affected routes for 60 minutes — that drops per-token compute and should eliminate the tail.

I've attached a short checklist with the exact flags and a diagnostics request. We'll follow up with a timeline and a root-cause note.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll make this right.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-12-05T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: BrightCommerce streaming incident — customer impact and credits

Looping in ops and finance for the customer impact and remediation credits. Summary: BrightCommerce observed degraded streaming response pacing causing increased time between token chunks and intermittent client timeouts. Jordan has applied routing and batching mitigations; customer is trying a client toggle and a temporary model downgrade.

Proposed customer-facing commitments to confirm with Jordan before we finalize: 
- Provide an incident timeline with root cause within 48 hours.
- Offer a 30% usage credit for affected daily volume during the window (we can scale down to 10% if the impact is smaller after analysis).
- Share the postmortem and action plan, including a sustained SLA adjustment for their most-critical routes if needed.

Please advise if ops needs additional telemetry or if finance needs a specific billing window for credits. Also recommend we include a short runbook BrightCommerce can keep in their ops playbook in case of recurrence (I drafted a client checklist — attached).

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Emily Torres <emily.torres@brightcommerce.com>, Daniel Park <ops@brightcommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-06T14:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Streaming responses slowed this morning

Emily / Daniel —

Update and commitments after 24 hours of analysis: thank you for your patience. We've confirmed the root cause and the corrective actions we took. TL;DR: a subset of us-west-2 edge proxies entered an unexpected token-emission backpressure state after a mesh config roll that increased ephemeral queueing under a particular traffic mix. That resulted in widened inter-token spacing for streaming responses.

What we did (summary):
- Immediate: traffic re-route to warmed shard pool, temporary token-batching relax, KV-cache touch hotfix (Dec 5, 09:35 PST).
- Recovery: rolled back the mesh config change and rebalanced the proxy pools (Dec 5, 12:10 PST).
- Validation: ran a canary across your production routes for 2 hours and saw median inter-token spacing drop from ~240ms to ~45ms; 99th percentile dropped from 2.8s to 220ms.

Customer commitments (what you'll see next):
- Root cause and full postmortem document by 2027-12-07T17:00:00-08:00 with timeline, impact metrics, and corrective controls.
- One-time credit applied to your Dec invoices equivalent to 30% of usage from 2027-12-05T08:40:00-2027-12-05T12:30:00 (billing will be adjusted within the week).
- A compact runbook we recommend adding to your SRE playbook (attached).

Short-term mitigation options still available if you see any residual effects:
- Client flag: set graceful-dechunking=true (one-line change).
- Fallback model: model-redwood-medium for 30–60 minutes.
- If you prefer us to maintain a warmed shard route for a longer window, we can schedule that for an hourly incremental cost (ops to confirm).

We're treating this as a priority to prevent recurrence: infra will add an automated probe for token-emission pacing and block mesh roll-forward when expanded queueing metrics are detected. I'll attach the postmortem link as soon as it's ready.

Apologies again for the customer impact — we appreciate the Clear and direct feedback and will keep you closely updated.

Best regards,
Jordan Blake
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
